label: Incident C
alert: checkout-api: Timeout acquiring a database connection (timeout=3000ms). HTTP 5xx is elevated. Investigate the cause and explain what distinguishes it from other plausible causes.
provenance: Synthetic evidence, authored for this controlled exercise. These records were not captured from a customer or a running cluster. Times and values form a consistent scenario, not a production benchmark.

evidence.title: Alert and timeline
evidence.content:
Environment: checkout-prod. Three application pods, one PostgreSQL cluster.
13:55 deployment checkout-api r184 began; complete at 13:57.
13:58 intermittent supplier failures observed. HTTP 5xx climbed gradually from 13:58, with p95=3400ms.
14:00 error: Timeout acquiring a database connection (timeout=3000ms).
Observation window: 13:45-14:05 UTC. Billing and inventory latency unchanged.

evidence.content:
checkout-1 measurements (other two pods show similar progression):
window,requests_per_second,pool_limit,pool_checked_out,active_db_queries,pool_waiters,db_query_p95_ms

At 14:00, 38 checked-out connections have no in-flight request owner. Pool size and request rate have no step change. Query durations remain stable.

evidence.content:
checkout-1 sample of completed requests:
request,connection_id,checkout,request_finished,connection_returned
q201,c21,13:58:02.010,13:58:02.842,NOT_OBSERVED_BY_14:05

Supplier-timeout requests finish without a corresponding pool-return event. Successful requests do return connections. Between 13:58 and 14:00 the cumulative checkout-minus-return count grows by 38 on checkout-1. These connections remain checked out after their request spans have ended.
